annotation.title_clean: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.title_en: Durkheim's Theory of the Division of Labor and Its Relevance for Socially Responsible Robotics
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 366 (Robophilosophy 2022), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2022 conference paper applying Durkheim's theory of the division of labor, and its three social pathologies (forced division, excessive division, anomie), to analyze the social and ethical impacts of workplace robots and to outline socially responsible robotics innovation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Durkheim's three social pathologies provide a framework for analyzing robots' social impacts in the workplace.
Robots can contribute to forced division of labor, excessive division of labor and anomie.
Organic solidarity depends on interdependence through the division of labor.
Proposes a form of socially responsible innovation informed by Durkheim.
